# FDG3076

> DO name event argument classes with the “EventArgs” suffix, as shown in the following example:

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 3.6.3 Names of Events.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1710
- Automatic fix: not applied automatically (the fix can break callers)
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test none
- Status: draft

CA1710 reports a class derived directly from System.EventArgs whose name does not end with EventArgs; with its default dotnet_code_quality.CA1710.exclude_indirect_base_types = true it does not report a class derived from another EventArgs class, such as CancelEventArgs (probe with SDK 10.0.402), so coverage is partial. Renaming a public type changes the public API, so the fix is breaking; CA1710 has no code fix.

## From the book

```csharp
public class ClickedEventArgs : EventArgs {
  int x;
  int y;
  public ClickedEventArgs (int x, int y) {
     this.x = x;
     this.y = y;
  }
  public int X { get { return x; } }
  public int Y { get { return y; } }
}
```
